tagline: Three miles along Mascoma Lake to the Shakers' Chosen Vale.
intro: Route 4A runs 3.2 miles out of Lebanon along the shore of Mascoma Lake, on the path the Enfield Shakers took, toward Shaker Bridge and the buildings and fields of their old village in the valley between the lake and Mount Assurance, a peak the community held sacred.

The Shakers came in 1793 and called the place Chosen Vale. They made brooms, buckets and spinning wheels, sold seeds, applesauce and maple syrup, and left in 1923. The La Salette missionaries bought most of the property in 1927, and when the order left Enfield in 2023 the museum acquired the rest.

moments.title: Shaker Bridge
moments.text: In 1849 the Shakers built a half-mile bridge across a narrow part of Mascoma Lake to get their goods to the railroad on the other side faster.

moments.title: Enfield Shaker Museum
moments.text: The Great Stone Dwelling, the largest Shaker building, gave men and women separate doors to separate quarters under one slate roof and now holds the museum's main exhibits.
